summary:
I’m delighted to hear from you, and impressed by your astute ability to track me down. Unfortunately I am living about 600 miles to the south from you; near Disneyland, as a matter of fact. You’re about the only person I knew up there willing to try to find out what happened to me, which is as follows: I flew to Canada in February of last year, made my two speeches, then decided to become a Canadian citizen. But homesickness made me return to the U.S. after two months, despite the fact that I got into something near and dear to me: work­ ing for a heroin rehab centre, about which I have written a new novel already sold to Doubleday—which makes my second new novel this year, and both to 
them. In addition to all this I am now (are you ready?) remarried, and just one week ago we had a little baby boy named Christopher. Both my wife Tessa and Christopher are home, now, and both are doing fine. It was a three-hour deliv­ ery. The doctor had said, “You’ve got four to six hours to time the contractions; don’t call me until then.” But I took Tessa right in to the hospital (I’d been rehearsing it for months), and it turned out to be a good idea. You mention in your letter that many changes have taken place in your life; what are those, and—I hope—are they for the better? I wish very much I could see you again because you brought me some joy and fun and hope at a time when I had few if any friends and needed a friend very badly.
